Help
How the AI sides set up — where their line sits and how hard they press. Difficulty still decides how good they are. ⚠️ The shapes are not equally effective, so this is picking an opponent rather than turning a dial.
Ice slides and takes a long time to stop. Mud grips badly and kills the roll.
Set the size, the corners, the goals and how lively the boards are, then save it. Your fields sit alongside the built-in ones everywhere — the picker, the map votes, replays and drills — because they are fields, not a separate mode.
Before the whistle: test your stick, stand on the side you want, and let bots fill the rest. Press Start to kick off. Cocktail always warms up so each seat can set which way is up. Controllers warms up only when a pad is connected; Everyone warms up on touch and keyboard too, with an on-screen Start. A controller can join a match already under way by pressing a button — see Joining late.
Plug a controller in during a match and a player walks out to the touchline. Walk up or down to the half you want, then press START — you come on at the next goal, on that side. The match grows to fit: a 3v3 that gains a player becomes a 4v4, with a bot added to the other side. Stand near the halfway line and you'll be put wherever Extra controllers says (opposite you for Versus, alongside for Co-op). Unplug and your body leaves by the same touchline gate, the sides even up again, and your goals stay on the scoresheet. At kickoff turns all of this off: seats are handed out once and a controller that wakes up mid-match waits for the next match.
Your side first (you, then your team-mates), then the opposition. Blank lines keep the default name. Applies to the next match.
Nobody crosses halfway until the ball is played — except inside the centre circle, which stays open so you can turn and pass back. Cross anywhere else and you're pushed home. Free-for-all once it's played.
One keeper and one attacker inside a goal box at a time — the net and the marked rectangle in front of it. Whoever gets there first holds the spot; anyone else gets half a second inside and is then eased back out, so you can run straight through without the pitch fighting you. Stops a team parking three bodies on their own line, and stops the attack burying the keeper under a scrum.
KICK stops being ball-only: a wall or a body in range takes the hit and you take the reaction. A wall has nothing to give, so kicking one launches you off it. Applies to everyone, bots included.

Your Player

Each seat keeps its own name, colour and face. Player 1 is you — your record, your unlocks and your leaderboard entry are always seat one, however many people are playing.
Only changes themes whose players have a front — Shrimp, VideoSoccer arrowheads. Off keeps your body pointing up the pitch, which some people find easier to track. A round theme (Pool, Mono) looks the same either way, and every theme draws a ring at your real size regardless.
Saved at 128×128 — the size it's actually drawn at, so it costs a few KB rather than the several megabytes a camera produces. It is never uploaded: the leaderboard only ever sees the word "photo".
Player

Options

Digital gives you eight directions and nothing between them, like a D-pad or the arrow keys: you are either holding a direction or you are not, and a half-push does not mean half speed. Analogue is the old behaviour, where how far you push is how fast you go. A diagonal runs at the same speed as a straight line either way. Controllers are always analogue — a real stick has an in-between and it should mean something.
Lower = push further for full speed
Every control, button and heading, and the words the pitch shouts. The longer help paragraphs stay in English — a hint that lies about what a setting does is worse than one you have to translate yourself. Automatic follows your device. Nothing you have typed is ever translated: your name, your maps and the scores stay exactly as they are.
An upright cabinet with four sets of controls, all wired to the keyboard the way an arcade encoder does it. Four people play against the AI, or two a side.
For a screen lying flat on a table with people stood around it. Tell it where each player is sitting and their "up" will point into the table instead of off the top of the screen.
Sideways = goals left and right. Auto only goes sideways on Steam Deck.
Separate tab puts these cards on /menu and leaves this page all game. Both stay in sync live.
There's a ⛶ in the top bar mid-match too. F11 works as usual.

Theme

A bundle sets every other tab in one go. Change any one of them and the theme becomes Custom — put them all back and its name comes straight back with them. A theme changes how the game looks; the pitch you play on is a separate choice under Match → Pitch. A few themes are drawn for one particular court and will switch you to it and say so, and you can change it back there afterwards.
A set fills in all six below at once. It's the same slot the Theme card shows.
Trap lets you hold KICK to carry the ball, then release to shoot. One-touch kicks the instant you touch it — faster, much less forgiving. How long you can carry is the Trap window slider below.
Holding KICK winds a shot up to +90% power, and a ring closes round you while it does. The slider is how long you have to hold for the full amount — shorter makes every shot hard, longer makes the wind-up something you commit to. Switch it off and every kick fires at exactly its normal strength, however long the button is down, which is what you want if you hold KICK to carry the ball. Affects shots, one-touches, body checks and booting the snail.
Letting go of the movement stick shoots, so you can play with one thumb. The KICK button keeps working either way.
Hold KICK to sprint. A ring round you drains like a clock while you run; let go and it fires the kick, the way holding KICK always has. Run the ring out and you are locked down to the tired speed until it has filled all the way back up — and it fills slower than it empties, so a sprint is something you spend. The ring is yours — bots do not sprint, because they hold KICK to trap rather than to run, and giving them the boost flattened the difficulty tiers into each other. Turn it off and holding KICK instead drags you down to a deliberate walk, which is how the game worked before this existed.
Tilt the phone and the pitch and the players shift by slightly different amounts, so the pitch reads as something you're looking into rather than a flat picture. About ten pixels at full tilt — enough to feel, not enough to fight. Neutral is wherever you're actually holding the phone, so it works lying down. Render only: it never moves the ball or a player, only where they're drawn. Off automatically if your system asks for reduced motion.
A short label over a player the moment they earn something the match record keeps — GOAL, ASSIST, SAVE, KEY PASS, CLEARANCE, SHOT, POST. It rises and fades in about a second. Touches are deliberately left out: everybody has them, so a label on every touch would be a permanent smear of text telling you nothing.
Maps the ball's pattern onto a sphere and rolls it along the way the ball is travelling, so the markings compress at the edge and go over the horizon instead of spinning flat. Render only — it never changes how the ball moves or bounces. Works with whichever ball look you have picked.
A freeze-frame on the strike, but only when you first-touch a shot that's actually going in — the game checks the ball's path before it gives you one. Also fires on the goal itself. Set to 0 for none. Independent of screen shake.
How hard the pad buzzes — on your own kick (harder the harder you hit it), the ball off the boards, the freeze-frame, and a goal, with the side that scored feeling it more. Set to 0 for none. Like hit stop this is not screen shake, so turning the wobble off leaves it alone. Needs a controller that reports a rumble motor; touch, the keyboard and an arcade panel have nothing to buzz.
On a goal the camera pushes in on whoever put it there. Drag it all the way down to off for no push at all. Speed is how long the push takes, so a smaller number is a faster push. It always drifts back out slowly, whatever you set here. This is the only thing that controls the push — it is separate from Screen shake & effects, so you can have one without the other.
How far back a goal replay begins — the build-up you see before the shot. Longer keeps more of the move that made the goal; shorter gets you back to the kickoff sooner. The ball hitting the net is always kept on the end.
Watch replays and the idle demo match from beside the touchline instead of straight down: the pitch turns so goal-to-goal runs left to right, the ground tilts away from you, and every player stands up off it as a cylinder with the ball a real sphere above its shadow. Render only — nothing about the match changes, and the two views replay the same recording. Deliberately not offered for playing a match in: a body in front of the ball is good television and a bad time on the ball.
Ball and player speed plus your current feel numbers, bottom-left while you play.

Updates
Tap to copy
Sheet
Set the game's defaults once in a Google Sheet and every device you open Magnetball on starts there — the pitch, the difficulty, the theme, the Game Feel sliders. It is read, never written, so nothing about this device leaves it. Anything you change here still wins over the sheet, unless the sheet is set to managed, which is how a cabinet or a venue is kept identical. Read at launch from a copy kept on the device, so it works offline; the button pulls a fresh one now. See LEADERBOARD_SETUP.md for the tab.
Magnetball is one web page with no accounts and no server: your player, settings, career and saved replays are stored on this device, and clearing site data clears them. It works offline once loaded.
There is no online play. Every mode here is local: against the bots, or with other people on the same screen — up to four with controllers, or two thumbs on one phone. If you want to play somebody who is not in the room, the closest thing is a saved replay: they re-render at full quality on any device and are about 25KB, so a match is something you can send.
Saves the whole game as a single HTML file. Open it in any browser — double-click it, or drag it onto a window — and it plays with no connection at all, on Linux, Mac or Windows. Your career and settings do not come with it: a file on your disk is a different origin to a website, so the browser keeps their saves apart. Put the file next to a copy of the assets folder if you want the flags, animals and pixel font as well; without it they fall back to drawn shapes and a system font.
Writes one .json file holding everything this device knows about you: every setting including Game Feel, your player, your record and unlocks, custom maps, drill times, and a season, tournament or Gauntlet run in progress. Open it on the other device with Import save and it takes over from what is there, then the page reloads. Saved replays and your photo library do not travel — they run to megabytes and would make a file you could not send; the photo you are wearing does. The update deadline is never imported, so a save from a device that had been offline for a month cannot bring a countdown with it.
Point a phone camera at the code and it opens this game. Everything is on the device it is opened on, so the other phone starts fresh — it is a quick way to hand somebody the game, not a way to share your save. Use Export save above for that.

Opens in its own tab or window — put it on the laptop screen and the game on the projector. Bookmark vj/ under the game’s address to go straight there.
Only the things worth knowing about: what was added, what changed in a way you will feel, and one line for the bug fixes.

Replays

Keeps every goal in the list above without you pressing anything — for showing the game to people, when stopping to save each one is the thing you cannot do. Saved here only, never downloaded; the oldest go when the list is full.
The last few matches are kept in full, kickoff to whistle, with no need to press anything — so a match somebody asks about afterwards is still there. They appear under Saved matches above and in your match history, and the oldest goes when the count is full. A whole match is roughly twenty times a single goal (about 0.8MB for a long one), which is why this is a count and not a switch; goals are capped separately, so neither pushes out the other.
Holds on the last frame when it ends, so you can watch it again or scrub back. Use ✕ on the bar to come back here.
A web page is never told where your browser puts downloads, so that is the usual place for this device rather than a path read off your disk — if your browser is set to ask each time, it is wherever you chose. Replays are saved from Save on the playback bar while you are watching one, and from Save goal replay and Save match replay on the result screen. They are deliberately not offered in the middle of a match.

VJ Mode

Two video decks, two DJ decks, and a background video — run from their own full-screen page while the game plays on the projector. Everything is off until you turn it on there, and the game looks and sounds exactly as normal until then.

SHOP

Cosmetics only · support the game

The honest bit ❤

Magnetball is free, and everything that touches gameplay stays free — no pay-to-win, no ads, no loot boxes. The shop is cosmetics only: a way to support the game if you're enjoying it. You can also unlock every cosmetic just by playing and showing up for the daily reward. Coins buy nothing that helps you win — only how your disc looks.

WATCH

Opens a saved replay, of one goal or of a whole match. It is the match data rather than a video — plain JSON — so it plays at your screen’s size and in whatever theme you are using now, and you can open it in any text editor.

ARCADE

Standup cabinet · four panels

Takings

Kept on this machine only — it is never sent anywhere. Free play still counts the games, because how much a cabinet gets used is worth knowing whether or not it is charging for it.
Coin-op needs a credit to start a game — press a coin key (5 to 8, one per player) to add one. Free play starts whenever somebody presses START.

Panel

MAME's own defaults, so a cabinet wired with any keyboard encoder works with no setup. Bound to the physical switch rather than the printed character, so the numpad stick and the coin keys never collide and the layout the machine is set to does not matter.

MAP MAKER

Build a field

Your fields

Saved on this device. They appear in the Field picker with everything else.

Shape

Rounded corners are an arc the ball rolls along; chamfered is a straight diagonal. Square is the ordinary rectangle. Held below whichever of the two halves is smaller, so the corners can never eat the whole pitch.

Goals

A wide mouth makes a shooting gallery and a narrow one makes a siege — the built-in fields all sit near a third of the width. A dead net kills the ball where it lands; a lively one spits it back out, which on a small pitch means the ball is never out of play.

Boards

How much speed the boards give back. 100% is a perfect rebound, so a pass off the wall arrives as fast as it left; below about 40% the boards absorb the game and it stops being a passing surface. Above 100% the walls add speed — a pinball table, and deliberately reachable, because it is a good time and nothing depends on it being sane.

CONTROLLER

Press a direction on your controller to bind it

Button map

Move stick

The game finds the stick by itself on almost every controller. If yours moves on the D-pad but not the stick, bind it here — you will be asked to push right, then down.

How to Play

🎯 Goal. Push the ball into the opponent's net. Most goals before the clock runs out wins.

🕹️ Move. Touch and drag anywhere on the right half — a joystick appears under your thumb. Drag to steer; further = faster.

👟 Trap & shoot. Hold KICK and run into the ball. It sticks to your feet while you line up, then let go to shoot the way you're facing — hold longer for a harder strike (the ring round your disc fills as it charges). A quick tap instead of a hold is an instant pass. How long you can carry is the Trap window slider in Game Feel; set Ball control to One-touch there and the ball fires the moment you touch it, which is faster and far less forgiving.

🧊 Hit stop. First-touch a shot that's genuinely going in and the game freezes for a beat on the strike — it checks the ball's path before it gives you one, so a shot that goes wide, hits a body or dies short gets nothing. A trapped-and-carried shot doesn't count; this is for the first touch. Length is the Hit stop slider in Game Feel, and it's separate from Screen shake.

🧲 Magnet. Off by default — the ball is a free puck. Ball magnet (Game Feel, 0–100) adds a passive stick that carries the ball at your feet without holding KICK. Most people leave it at 0.

⏱ Kickoff. Both teams hold their own half until the ball is played. The centre circle is a gate: stand in it and you may cross the line early, so you can turn and pass backwards instead of only forwards. Stray over the line anywhere else and you're pushed back. Turn the whole rule off in the Match card.

🏆 Ranked. Matches against bots earn RP and climb the ladder (Wood → Legend); harder bots are worth more. Training is free practice with no clock. A timed game that's level at the whistle goes to sudden-death overtime — first goal wins.

🐌 Killer Lobsters. Two balls at once. The normal one scores as usual and re-serves from the centre, but nothing else resets — no kickoff, players hold position. The second is the snail: huge, heavy, and it can only be shoved, never kicked. Push it into their goal and the match ends there and then, whatever the score.

🧊 Surfaces. Grass grips. Ice slides and takes an age to stop. Mud grabs and kills the roll. Both wear in as you play — mud churns and ice picks up skate cuts where the traffic is.

👥 2-Player. Lay the phone flat between you. Player 1 uses the bottom controls, Player 2 the top (rotated) ones.

🎮 Controllers. Set Input to Controllers and connect gamepads (press a button to wake them). Each pad takes a seat — you first, then an opponent, then a teammate — so 2 pads is 1v1, 8 pads a full 4v4. Left stick moves, A / RT kicks. Empty seats stay bots. Extra controllers → Co-op fills your side first instead.

🤚 One hand. Game Feel → One-handed. Letting go of the movement stick shoots where you were heading, so you can play with one thumb. The KICK button still works.

⚙ Settings elsewhere. Display → Settings location → Separate tab moves every setting to /menu and leaves this page all game. Both stay in sync live, and that tab shows a running readout of ball and player speed.
